findings.problem: The vendors module parses If-Match three ways: service.py:91 expected_version (sets checks.problem=if_match_required, no whitespace strip), questionnaire.py:46 expected_version (same name, strips whitespace, omits checks.problem), and an inline copy in service.py:399-410 put_sensitive. A missing If-Match on a questionnaire PATCH returns a 400 without the if_match_required code that every other vendor write and every other module (identity, requisitions, projects, sourcing, purchasing) returns. The same split holds for stale(): service.py:107 builds the ProblemError by hand, questionnaire.py:60 uses conflict() with different detail text. Two cursor codecs (service.py:115, performance.py:80) also differ in error code (invalid_cursor vs the default). No client branches on these today, so this is drift, not breakage.
findings.fix: Keep one expected_version/stale pair in service.py (or a vendors-local helper module), import it in questionnaire.py and use it in put_sensitive; delete the copies.
